transport: VE.Can, RJ45 · CAN bus carrying NMEA 2000 · GX CAN-bus profile must be set to 'VE.Can & Lynx Ion BMS (250kbit/s)' (Settings → Services → VE.Can port) · daisy chain, RJ45 bus terminator required at the first and last device · N2K device class: Electrical generation, device function: Battery · NMEA 2000 reached via a VE.Can-to-NMEA2000 micro-C cable · no slave id; multiple units are separated by VE.
blocks: Supported NMEA 2000 PGNs, identical in both manuals: 126996 Product Information · 127506 DC Detailed Status · 127508 DC/Battery Status · 127501 Switch Bank Status, with Status 1 = Contactor, Status 2 = Alarm, Status 3 = Battery voltage low, Status 4 = Battery voltage high, Status 5 = Programmable relay status
sharedMapEvidence: TWO separate vendor manuals print an identical map. Lynx Smart BMS manual rev 17 (01/2026) §11.2 and Lynx Smart BMS NG manual rev 14 (07/2026) §9.2 both carry a table headed 'Supported NMEA 2000 PGNs' listing the same four PGNs — 126996, 127506, 127508, 127501 — in the same order, with the same five Switch Bank Status assignments spelled identically (Contactor / Alarm / Battery voltage low / Batte
gotchas: THE PGN FIELD LAYOUTS ARE NOT IN ANY VICTRON DOCUMENT. Both manuals name the four PGNs and stop. Field offsets, widths, scales and resolutions for 126996 / 127506 / 127508 / 127501 live in the NMEA 2000 standard, which is a paid document. The reports list above is drawn from the manuals' own parameter-availability tabl

'VE.Can & Lynx Ion BMS (250kbit/s)' is a bus-profile name, not evidence of a register map. The committed docs/victron-ve-can-registers-v20.pdf (VREGS v20, 2015) defines BMS registers 0x0370 BMS Flags, 0x0371 BMS State, 0x0372 BMS Error flags — and marks each 'NOTE: This message is only implemented in the Lynx Ion'. The

VE.Can and BMS-Can cannot be combined on the same bus, and the Lynx Smart BMS must go on the GX's VE.Can port, NOT its BMS-Can port. The manual calls this out as a specific failure mode. Two separate buses need a GX with two, each with two terminators.
Do not hand-make the RJ45 cables. Manual rev 17: 'always use "manufactured" RJ45 UTP cables. Do not manufacture these cables yourself.'

Multiple Lynx BMSes on one VE.Can network with the SAME instance are treated by the GX as one parallel-redundant virtual battery and collapsed into a single device. If you want them separate you must assign unique VE.Can instances by hand. A driver counting devices will miscount otherwise.
unmappedReports: Allowed to charge / Allowed to discharge (ATC / ATD) — the two booleans that gate everything a rules engine might do, and there is no wire name for either., Mode and State (BMS operational state) — no MetricKind., Relay status (programmable relay) — no second-output slot., Contactor state (PGN 127501 Status 1) — this is 'is the bank physically connected'. switch-state is the closest wire name but is semantically the load output elsewhere in this catalogue., Balancer status, individual cell voltages, min/max cell voltage, min/max cell temperature — no MetricKind., Number of batteries, number of cells, number in series, number in parallel — bank topology, no MetricKind., Deepest discharge, cumulative Ah drawn, discharged energy, charged energy, synchronisations, number of full discharges, min/max battery voltage, last error — history records, not instantaneous metrics., Lynx Distributor fuse status (up to 4 modules) — no MetricKind for 'a fuse blew'.
